facts.text: Indian River Estates sits in a county that once grew pineapples, and the former plantation is now a museum bequeathed to the Historical Society by Ruth Hallstrom.
The Hallstrom House, a 1918 landmark listed on the National Registry of Historic Places, is just a short drive from Indian River Estates.
The Indian River Citrus Museum, a historic site that showcases the region’s citrus heritage, is located near Indian River Estates.
The Indian River County Historical Society, headquartered near Indian River Estates, focuses on restoring and preserving historic sites throughout the county.
The Historical Society’s collection includes over 7,000 photographs, offering a visual history of Indian River County and its communities.
Indian River County’s first library, the Marian Fell Library, opened as a pioneering institution for women’s suffrage and remains open today.
